args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18 across us-east, us-west, and eu-west). Per the platform runbook, I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions. Post-rollback status: all three regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 remains unhealthy in production and should not be redeployed until it is fixed. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy (staging only) and was not involved in this rollback. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before re-releasing.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened a SEV2 incident. The on-call engineer has been paged.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent production release that was healthy. v2.3.1 was unhealthy in production, and v2.3.1-rc was only in staging. Because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production, no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Current state:** Every region is on v2.3.0, healthy, with the error rate down from 0.18 to 0.002.
- **Incident:** It is SEV2 and describes the failure, the rollback, and the post-rollback state. It also notes that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the failure is fixed.

I did not investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure.

The rollback worked and checkout-api is healthy again. Now I'll open the incident.
